description:
FILED s476 (Fable, 2026-09-07) -- USER ask: "please add a note about setting `$ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}` or something similar.  Document it too.  So code can verify that they are running in PCL.  No hurry, anytime the coming days."  (Checked: never noted before -- no task, no DECIDED/README/ir-spec mention.)

WHY: there is NO honest signal today.  `$^V`/`$]` answer 5.30.0 (compatibility), `$^X` DELIBERATELY points at real perl (so spawned subprocesses run perl), `$^O` is the OS.  A test file, a module or a user script that must behave differently under PCL (skip a row, avoid a not-supported construct, report) has nothing to ask.

WHAT: the PCL runtime makes `$ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}` TRUE in every PCL process (the USER`s spelling; the leading/trailing underscores mark it as an OUTPUT set by the runtime, distinct from the `PCL_*` INPUT knobs `PCL_OPT`, `PCL_CACHE_DIR`, `PCL_NO_CORE`...).  VALUE = PCL`s version as `pcl --version` prints it (an installed tree reads <root>/VERSION; a checkout answers whatever `pcl --version` answers there -- find it, do not invent a second version source), so the variable is a flag AND says which PCL.  Usage the docs show:
    if ($ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}) { ... }            # running under PCL
    print "PCL $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}\n";           # e.g. PCL 0.1.0

RULED (Fable, at filing) -- CHILD PROCESSES MUST NOT INHERIT IT: `$^X` is real perl, so a `system($^X, ...)` / backtick / piped-open / exec child that inherited the variable would believe it runs under PCL -- a silent wrong of the worst kind (a PCL child sets its own).  Therefore the variable is NOT put into the process environment with setenv: PCL`s %ENV is a live view of `sb-ext:posix-environ` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~11419/11463 read it per access; writes go through sb-posix:setenv ~18266 so libc sees TZ), and the entry is SYNTHETIC at that read layer -- present in `$ENV{...}`, `exists`, `keys %ENV`, `each`, `%ENV` copies (`my %e = %ENV`), absent from `sb-ext:posix-environ` and hence from every child and from `system("env")`.  Assignment / `delete $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}` behave as for any key (a deleted synthetic key stays deleted for the process; a written one is written for real -- say which and probe both; the simplest sound shape wins).  If the %ENV accessors turn out to be ONE helper the seeding is one arm; if they are several, ONE predicate they all ask (rule 11).  Rule 12: no other synthetic key -- a closed set of one, named in the code comment.

DOCUMENT (the USER: "Document it too"): README (a short `Detecting PCL from Perl code` paragraph near the caches/knobs section -- the variable, its value, that children do not inherit it, and why `$^X`/`$^V` are NOT the signal); `docs/ir-spec.md` (normative, the magic-globals / %ENV section: the name, the value contract, the synthetic-not-inherited rule); `pcl --help` if it lists the environment knobs (one line, marked as set BY pcl).

GUARDS (Pl/t, a new `pcl-runtime-env-01.t` or the file that owns %ENV rows): (1) `$ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}` true and equal to `pcl --version`s string -- NOT an oracle-compared transpile row (perl prints undef by design): `run_cl` with an explicit expectation; (2) `exists`/`keys` see it; (3) a REAL-PERL child `system($^X, "-e", q{exit(exists $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_} ? 1 : 0)})` exits 0 -- the non-inheritance row; (4) a PCL child (`runpcl`/`pcl` as $^X-substitute) sees its OWN; (5) `delete` / assignment per the chosen semantics.  Inverse-verified on the base extraction.

SIZE: S (runtime %ENV reader + version source + docs + guards).  Runtime-only, no gen bump, `cl/` change -> the full sweep + the companion io/ + op/magic.t + op/exec.t legs.  SCHEDULED: a filler in the next correctness brief with room -- appended to s473h (the singletons brief) by Fable s476; may ride any earlier brief that finishes its members with time left.

=== DONE (s473h, Opus, 2026-09-08) ===
SHIPPED exactly as designed.  $ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_} is true in every PCL process
and carries `pcl --version`'s version string, read from the SAME source (an
installed tree's VERSION file, else `git describe`) lazily and memoized, so a
program that never reads it pays nothing.

SYNTHETIC at the %ENV read layer: present in $ENV{}, exists, keys, values,
each and every %ENV copy; absent from sb-ext:posix-environ, so a real-perl
child does NOT inherit it (probed: system($^X, "-e", ...) exits 0, and the key
is absent from `env` output) and a PCL child sets its own (probed).

Rule 12: a CLOSED SET OF ONE, named in the code.  Rule 11: the accessors are
several -- p-gethash, p-keys, p-values, %p-exists-p, p-delete, the three
`local $ENV{...}` helpers and the wholesale `%ENV = LIST` -- so they share ONE
predicate (%p-runtime-env-synthetic-p) and ONE value (%p-pcl-version); `each`
and %p-marker-pairs (and so every %ENV copy) are covered for free, being built
on p-keys + p-gethash.

A REAL environment variable of that name always WINS, which is what makes
assignment an ordinary %ENV write (it exports, as %ENV always does); delete, a
wholesale replacement and `local` all hide the synthetic entry.

DOCUMENTED: README ("Detecting PCL from Perl code"), `pcl --help`'s
Environment section (marked as set BY pcl), docs/ir-spec.md's magic-globals
table (normative, including "a translator emitting for a different host MUST
rename it").

GUARD: NEW Pl/t/pcl-runtime-env-01.t, 12 rows, 0.8 s wall; inverse-verified on
an a9f2a264 extraction (rows 1-4, 7, 10-11 fail there; 5, 6, 8, 9 and 12 are
the negatives that must keep passing).  Commit fa09c143.

FOUND AND FIXED ALONGSIDE: #1392 -- `scalar(%ENV)` answered HASH(0x1) where
perl answers the key count, because the MARKER *is* the hash (#736) and
p-scalar had no arm for it.
subject: USER ask (s476, 2026-09-07): `$ENV{_PCL_RUNTIME_}` = PCL`s version string in every PCL process, so Perl code can verify it runs under PCL (no honest signal today: $^V says 5.30.0, $^X is real perl) -- SYNTHETIC at the %ENV read layer so real-perl CHILDREN do not inherit it; document in README + ir-spec; guards incl. the child-does-not-see-it row; size S, no hurry
